column1: # wt148 · PROMISES ADJUDICATED — one row per (sentence, named artefact) that scripts/wt148_promise_sweep.py
# emits for an in-scope manuscript. A row is a CLAIM: that a human RAN OR READ the artefact and found
# the sentence borne out (or not). It is not a claim that the sentence looks fine.
# HOW TO FALSIFY A ROW — and you should, because a row nobody re-checks is worth nothing:
#   1. Take the row's `evidence` column. It names a command to run or a file to read.
#   2. Run it or read it. If it does not show what `note` says it shows, the row is FALSE.
#   3. Delete the row. `python3 scripts/wt148_promise_sweep.py` goes RED on the next run, because the
#      promise it covered becomes unadjudicated. That is how this file is audited rather than trusted.
#   Editing the SENTENCE also invalidates the row: `promise_id` is a hash of (paper, artefact,
#   sentence), so a reworded promise gets a new id and the old row is reported STALE. Re-check, do not
#   H  HELD       — the artefact bears the sentence out.
#   N  NOT A PROMISE — the sentence names the artefact but asserts nothing about it that could fail
#                   independently of a row adjudicated elsewhere. Still checked; still a row.
#   R  REPAIRED   — the artefact did NOT bear it out; the manuscript was changed in the same pass, and
#                   `note` says what failed and which script repaired it.
#   C  CARDED     — failed, not repairable in-pass; `note` carries a NAMED FALSIFIER.
# SCOPE. The line below is the gate. Adding a manuscript stem to it turns the sweep red until every
# promise that manuscript emits carries a row. Widening scope is a data edit, deliberately.
